rites.name: Lyanys
rites.text: Lyanys is the concept of Zephessith's first sounding, the hum that condensed the world's roots in the undated Singing. It is less a being than a resonance that rings through the forming stars and binds their drifting matter into the first lasting shapes.

rites.name: Kruthun
rites.text: Kruthun is the concept of a rising, sounding root-tone that spread through Zephessith during the Singing, when the first roots of the world condensed out of silence. It is remembered as the force that taught the early groves to hold their shape against the drift of the void.

rites.name: Venioniel
rites.text: Venioniel is the concept of resonance itself as it appeared in Zephessith's Singing, the sounding by which the first roots of the world condensed out of silence. Across the Holy Age, temples and orders carried its tones through flame and ritual, believing each struck note bound another root into the world.

rites.name: Shazyusora
rites.text: Shazyusora is the concept of a rite in Zephessith's Courts, in which a petitioner is weighed against the gravity of their own oath before a council of judges. It is the principle by which the doors between worlds are measured and sealed, so that each threshold holds only what its keepers have agreed to bear.

rites.name: Grazhuktak
rites.text: Grazhuktak is a concept of the Courts of Zephessith, a mind-form of the trial-law that the councils used to judge which doorways between worlds could stand. It is said to hold a single unbroken oath that no hand has ever been able to break.

rites.name: Krogar
rites.text: Krogar is the concept of the Seeding in Zephessith, the quiet hour when the makers sow the Weave into the stellar lanes and the old powers lie dormant. It is less a being than the stillness itself, a pause in which the sky waits to learn what it will become.

rites.name: Teornausia
rites.text: Teornausia is the concept of a chain of holding walls that Zephessith's orders raised across centuries of the Walled Age, each wall keeping a grove or kingdom from its neighbours. Its doctrine holds that a boundary is a kind of promise, and that a sovereign who breaks one breaks the world's trust. Its first crossings are remembered as the moment the Age of the first sovereign began.

rites.name: Ashasora
rites.text: Ashasora is the concept of the shared walls that held Zephessith's cities together through the Walled Age, a bond kept by the orders and churches that tended the stone. In the Age of Sundering it became the idea that a people could be split from its own earth, and every crossing afterward was measured against it.

rites.name: Theisora
rites.text: Theisora is a rite-event in Zephessith during the Holy Age, when temples kindle sacred flame to force the ending to branch and the Library to shelve each outcome. The branching lasts only moments but reshapes which futures remain open for the age's orders.

rites.name: Kalunarira
rites.text: Kalunarira is the concept of the branching ending in Zephessith, the moment a single future splits into many and the Library shelves each outcome. In the Holy Age, when temples and flame orders governed the sky, its name was spoken as a warning against settling any question too early.

rites.name: Amiantollor
rites.text: Amiantollor is a concept that exists in the Three Futures of Zephessith, where the ending branches and the Library shelves each outcome as its own volume. It appears during the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke the old bonds between peoples and the lands they once held.
